subject: phys
title: Make the Bulb Light Up
question: What does a bulb need to light up?

steps.title: Parts of a circuit
steps.text: A circuit is a path that electricity flows around. This one has four parts. The battery pushes the electricity. The wires carry it. The bulb lights up when electricity flows through it. The switch turns the circuit on and off.
steps.try: Drag the picture to look at each part from all sides.
steps.see: The moving dots show electricity flowing out of the battery, along the wires, through the bulb and back to the battery.

steps.title: A complete loop
steps.text: Electricity can only flow if the circuit is a complete loop, with no gaps. One wire has come loose from the battery. Now there is a gap, so nothing flows and the bulb stays dark.
steps.try: Press Plug the wire in, then press Unplug it.
steps.see: The bulb lights only when every part is joined up in one unbroken loop, from one end of the battery all the way round to the other.

steps.title: The switch
steps.text: A switch is a safe way to make a gap in a circuit and then close it again. When the switch is off, its metal arm is lifted up, so the loop has a gap. When the switch is on, the arm touches the metal contact and the loop is complete.
steps.try: Press Switch on and Switch off.
steps.see: Switch off opens a gap and the bulb goes out. Switch on closes the gap and the bulb lights. The light switches in your home work in the same way.

steps.title: Test a material
steps.text: Now the circuit has a test gap held by two clips. We can put different things across the gap. If a thing lets electricity through, the loop is complete and the bulb lights.
steps.try: Put each object across the gap. Guess first: will the bulb light?
steps.see: The metal spoon, the coin and the paper clip make the bulb light. The plastic ruler, the wooden stick, the rubber eraser and the paper do not.

steps.title: Conductors and insulators
steps.text: Materials that let electricity flow through them are called conductors. Most metals are good conductors. Materials that stop electricity are called insulators. Plastic, rubber, dry wood and dry paper are insulators. A wire has metal inside to carry the electricity and a plastic coat outside to keep it safely inside.
steps.try: Press Sort them to put each object in the right group.
steps.see: Every object made of metal is a conductor. Everything else here is an insulator.

steps.title: Two batteries
steps.text: Add a second battery in the loop, joined end to end with the first one. Two batteries push the electricity harder, so more flows and the bulb shines brighter. Stay safe: only ever use small batteries like these. Never play with plugs or wall sockets. The electricity there is strong enough to badly hurt you.
steps.try: Turn the second battery on and off.
steps.see: With two batteries the dots move faster and the bulb is brighter. Too many batteries would burn the bulb out.

quiz.q: Which circuit will make the bulb light up?
options: A loop with a gap in it
A complete loop with no gaps
A bulb joined to a battery by one wire
quiz.why: Electricity needs an unbroken path from the battery, through the bulb and back to the battery.

quiz.q: Which of these is a conductor?
quiz.why: Metals let electricity flow through them. Rubber and wood are insulators.

quiz.q: What happens when you switch the switch off?
options: It makes a gap in the loop, so the bulb goes out
quiz.why: Switching off lifts the metal arm and breaks the loop, so electricity stops flowing.
